subtitle: When the northern wheel of empire met the southern wall of a river

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a king on horseback before a broad river, distant armies faint on opposite banks
panels.action: Pulakeshin II sits tall on a warhorse at the stony southern bank of the Narmada, one hand raised as if to halt the far-off northern host across the wide gleaming river under a vast Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: Pulakeshin II of Vatapi stands at the Narmada, where Harsha’s northern power meets the southern stone of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: वातापी का पुलकेशिन द्वितीय नर्मदा पर खड़ा है, जहाँ हर्ष की उत्तरी सत्ता दक्कन की चट्टान से भिड़ती है।

panels.shot: broad aerial of the Indian subcontinent with rivers and regions softly picked out
panels.action: A map-like view of the subcontinent unfolds in earthy colors, with the Ganga–Yamuna heartland, the Narmada line and the Deccan plateau subtly marked by rivers, forests and faint city clusters instead of borders.

dialogue.text: In the seventh century, the land from Punjab to the eastern seas trembles under new lords, new monasteries, and new courts hungry for fame.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी में, पंजाब से पूरब की लहरों तक धरती नए स्वामियों, नए मठों और यश-प्यासे दरबारों से काँप उठती है।

panels.shot: mid-wide of a ceremonial court scene with a northern emperor on a throne, back half-turned to us
panels.action: In a northern court, a tall, composed king robed in simple yet regal cloth sits on a lion-backed throne, ministers and monks arrayed around him beneath fluttering parasols and hanging bells.

dialogue.text: To the north, Harsha of Kanauj gathers fractured realms into a loose garland, binding princes by diplomacy, monks by gifts, and armies by restless hope.

i18n.hi: उत्तर में कन्नौज का हर्षा बिखरे राज्यों को ढीली माला में गूँथता है – राजाओं को कूटनीति से, भिक्षुओं को दान से, सेनाओं को बेचैन आशा से बाँधता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior of a southern court in Vatapi, with emphasis on inscriptional stele and temple silhouettes beyond
panels.action: Within a pillared hall in Vatapi, stone beams frame distant temple shikharas; a court scribe kneels before an unfinished stone slab, chiseling early Nagari lines under the watchful gaze of unseen nobles.

dialogue.text: Far to the south, the Chalukyas of Vatapi hold the rocky Deccan, their kings carving power into stone, temple and inscription.

i18n.hi: बहुत दक्षिण में, वातापी के चालुक्य पथरीला दक्कन थामे हैं – उनके राजा शक्ति को पत्थर, मंदिर और शिलालेख में उकेरते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle three-quarter of young Pulakeshin II in court, half in shadow, as elders argue in the background
panels.action: A younger Pulakeshin II stands slightly apart in the Vatapi hall, face calm but intent, while older nobles gesture and debate around the throne, some wary, some hopeful, the light catching the hilt of his sword.

dialogue.text: Pulakeshin, son of Kirtivarman, rises amid family rivalries and sceptical feudatories, earning his mantle by grasping both sword and council seat with steady hands.

i18n.hi: कीर्तिवर्मन का पुत्र पुलकेशिन, घर की कलह और शंकालु सामंतों के बीच उठता है, तलवार और सभा–भाषण दोनों से अपना हक कमा लेता है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of Pulakeshin II atop a fort wall, gesturing over the Deccan plains with hills and rivers spreading out
panels.action: Pulakeshin II stands on a high stone parapet, wind tugging at his cloak, as he looks out over rolling black-rock hills, winding rivers and scattered settlements of the Deccan below.

dialogue.text: From Konkan coasts to the interiors of Maharashtra and Karnataka, he welds chiefs to his banner, turning a regional power into a Deccan kingdom.

i18n.hi: कोंकण तट से लेकर महाराष्ट्र–कर्नाटक के भीतर तक, वह सरदारों को अपने ध्वज से जोड़ता है, एक प्रांतीय ताकत को दक्कनी राज्य बना देता है।

panels.shot: medium of a northern messenger presenting a scroll before Harsha, with a map unrolled on low table
panels.action: In Harsha’s court, a messenger bows with a palm-leaf bundle while a minister unfurls a painted map on a low table, the Narmada drawn as a bold dark line between north and south.

dialogue.text: News reaches Kanauj: a Chalukya king commands horses, elephants, hill-forts and coasts, and does not bend his neck to northern summons.

i18n.hi: खबर कन्नौज पहुँचती है – एक चालुक्य राजा घोड़े, हाथी, दुर्ग और तटों का मालिक है, और उत्तर की आज्ञा पर गर्दन नहीं झुकाता।

panels.shot: wide of Xuanzang observing a court from a modest corner, taking notes
panels.action: The monk Xuanzang sits cross-legged near a court pillar, simple robes contrasting with jeweled courtiers, as he quietly scribes notes and watches the king receive gifts and petitions.

dialogue.text: A Chinese pilgrim, Xuanzang, will later write of a mighty southern king whose realm Harsha cannot command, hinting at limits beneath imperial praise.

i18n.hi: एक चीनी यात्री, श्वेनसांग, बाद में लिखेगा उस दक्षिणी सम्राट के बारे में, जिसकी भूमि पर हर्ष का हुक्म नहीं चलता – प्रशंसा के नीचे सीमा की झलक छोड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: intimate court interior in Vatapi with Pulakeshin II and poet Ravikirti seated near a pillar, scrolls between them
panels.action: Pulakeshin II sits informally on a low seat beside a learned poet, who holds a palm-leaf manuscript; both bend over a rough map traced in powder on the floor, the river line drawn bold.

dialogue.text: In Vatapi, Pulakeshin listens to his brahmans and poets; they know the strength of rivers, forts and words, and whisper of Harsha’s long arm reaching south.

i18n.hi: वातापी में पुलकेशिन अपने ब्राह्मणों और कवियों को सुनता है; वे नदियों, किलों और शब्दों की ताकत जानते हैं, और फुसफुसाते हैं हर्ष के लंबे हाथ के दक्षिण तक बढ़ने की।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Pulakeshin II’s face as he contemplates, background fading to a mental map of the Narmada
panels.action: A close view of Pulakeshin II’s thoughtful face, his eyes lowered; behind him, faintly overlaid, lies the imagined curve of the Narmada, with small marks for ghats, ferries and forts.

dialogue.speaker: pulakeshin_ii
dialogue.text: A river is a wall only if guarded. Let the Narmada be ours.

i18n.hi: नदी तभी दीवार है जब पहरा हो। नर्मदा हमारी ढाल बने।

panels.shot: wide of Pulakeshin II inspecting the Narmada bank with officers, pointing to key crossing points
panels.action: On the rocky southern bank of the Narmada, Pulakeshin II walks with officers and local chiefs, pointing toward a shallow ford where carts cross, while boatmen watch curiously from moored craft.

dialogue.text: He strengthens the frontier: forts near fords, alliances with local clans, patrols along ghats where traders and pilgrims drift between worlds.

i18n.hi: वह सीमा को कड़ा करता है – घाटों के पास किले, स्थानीय कुलों से संधि, उन घाटों पर गश्त जहाँ व्यापारी और यात्री दो दुनियाओं के बीच बहते हैं।

panels.shot: mid-wide of northern troops assembling on open plain, standards bearing Harsha’s emblems, no direct combat
panels.action: On a broad northern plain, ranks of infantry, horsemen and elephants stand in ordered lines, banners fluttering with Harsha’s emblems as officers confer near a drum platform.

dialogue.text: Harsha prepares a southern venture; his armies, seasoned by campaigns in the north and east, look now toward the stone spine of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: हर्ष दक्षिण की चढ़ाई सँवारता है; उत्तर और पूरब के युद्धों से तपे उसके सैनिक अब दक्कन की पत्थरीली रीढ़ की ओर देखते हैं।

panels.shot: broad landscape of the Narmada valley, with two distant camps on opposite banks and haze between
panels.action: A hazy view of the Narmada valley shows two sprawling camps facing each other across the water, smoke from cookfires rising on both banks as the river glints between like a patient, watching eye.

dialogue.text: Sometime around 618, northern and southern hosts gaze at each other across the Narmada, their banners reflected in the slow brown water.

i18n.hi: लगभग ६१८ के आसपास, उत्तर और दक्षिण की सेनाएँ नर्मदा के दो किनारों से एक–दूसरे को तकती हैं, उनके ध्वज सुस्त भूरे जल में झिलमिलाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium of Pulakeshin II on the southern bank with retainers, mounted, facing unseen northern side
panels.action: Pulakeshin II sits firmly astride his horse on the southern bank, retainers arrayed behind him, his gaze steady across the unseen northern shore as wind ripples his standard.

dialogue.text: Chalukya memory will sing of a clash. Yet the stones and foreign eyes remember instead a line held, a push checked at water’s edge.

i18n.hi: चालुक्य स्मृति इसे भिड़ंत कहेगी; पर पत्थर और विदेशी आँखें एक थमी हुई रेखा याद रखती हैं – पानी के किनारे पर रुकी हुई चढ़ाई।

panels.shot: tight on the river’s surface between two banks, oars and reflections, no fighting, only tension
panels.action: The frame lingers on the river itself, oars resting in small boats, ripples distorting the mirrored hints of banners on either bank, the air heavy with unseen negotiations and calculation.

dialogue.text: We do not see the full exchange of blows or words; we know only that Harsha’s authority stops here, while Vatapi’s reach holds firm to the south.

i18n.hi: हम पूरी मारकाट या संवाद नहीं देखते; बस इतना जानते हैं कि हर्ष की हद यहाँ थमती है, और वातापी की पकड़ दक्षिण में जमी रहती है।

panels.shot: interior of Aihole temple hall with Ravikirti reciting before an audience, inscription stone behind him
panels.action: In a temple hall at Aihole, the poet Ravikirti stands before gathered courtiers and ascetics, gesturing gracefully as behind him a stone slab bears freshly carved, orderly lines of Sanskrit.

dialogue.text: Years later at Aihole, Ravikirti shapes this frontier into verse, saying Pulakeshin dashed Harsha’s joy like spray against the river rocks.

i18n.hi: सालों बाद ऐहोले में रविकीर्‍ति इस सीमा को कविता में ढालता है – कहता है, पुलकेशिन ने हर्ष की खुशी को नदी की चट्टानों पर टूटती छींट की तरह चूर कर दिया।

panels.shot: close-up of the Aihole inscription face, with selective emphasis on lines mentioning Harsha
panels.action: A close view of the Aihole inscription shows precise characters incised in stone, the section referring to Harsha subtly highlighted by shallow shadows on the carved lines.

dialogue.text: The prashasti is praise, not plain report; its sharp phrases guard Pulakeshin’s honour as much as his forts guard his rivers.

i18n.hi: यह प्रशस्ति है, सीधी खबर नहीं; इसकी तेज पंक्तियाँ पुलकेशिन की इज़्जत को वैसे ही बचाती हैं जैसे उसके किले उसकी नदियों को।

panels.shot: mid-wide of Xuanzang writing by lamplight, a small map of India beside him, Narmada line marked
panels.action: Xuanzang sits by an oil lamp, brush in hand, as he writes on a long scroll; beside him lies a rough sketch of India, with the Narmada drawn and the Deccan kingdom marked apart from Harsha’s realm.

dialogue.text: In distant Chang’an, Xuanzang’s record quietly confirms: the southern king holds his land, and Harsha does not rule beyond the great river.

i18n.hi: दूर चांग’आन में श्वेनसांग की तसलियों में एक शांत पुष्टि है – दक्षिण का राजा अपनी धरती थामे है, और महान नदी के पार हर्ष का राज नहीं चलता।

panels.shot: epic wide of Pulakeshin II returning in triumph to Vatapi, city on hill, people lining the road
panels.action: Pulakeshin II rides into Vatapi through stone gates, citizens lining the road, monks and merchants watching together as the king raises his hand in acknowledgment, the hill-fort rising solid behind him.

dialogue.text: For Vatapi, the Narmada stand becomes a pillar of pride; their king is the one who held the northern tide at the river.

i18n.hi: वातापी के लिए नर्मदा पर यह डट जाना गर्व का खंभा बनता है – उनका राजा वही है जिसने नदी पर उत्तर की लहर रोक दी।

panels.shot: contemplative medium of Pulakeshin II in a quiet temple courtyard, hand resting on a stone railing, river faintly imagined behind him
panels.action: In a quiet temple courtyard, Pulakeshin II stands by a stone railing, head slightly bowed, as if hearing distant river sounds; the carved Nandi beside him seems to share his calm, watchful strength.

dialogue.text: Yet frontiers held today are tested tomorrow; Pulakeshin knows rivers can shift, alliances can dry, and the Deccan’s peace is never still for long.

i18n.hi: पर जो सरहद आज थामी जाए, कल आज़माई जाती है; पुलकेशिन जानता है नदियाँ रुख बदलती हैं, संधियाँ सूख जाती हैं, और दक्कन की शांति कभी देर तक स्थिर नहीं रहती।

panels.shot: final aerial of the Narmada flowing through time, with faint overlays of different-age maps along its course
panels.action: An aerial view shows the Narmada winding through forests and rocky gorges, faint translucent outlines of different historical maps overlapping its course as if ages pass above its steady flow.

dialogue.text: Because Pulakeshin held the Narmada line, the Deccan stayed its own world for a time—and a river’s course became the border of an age.

i18n.hi: क्योंकि पुलकेशिन ने नर्मदा की रेखा थामी, दक्कन कुछ समय अपनी ही दुनिया बना रहा – और एक नदी का बहाव एक युग की सीमा बन गया।

title_i18n.en: Pulakeshin II Holds the Narmada Line

subtitle_i18n.en: When the northern wheel of empire met the southern wall of a river
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब उत्तर का चक्र टकराया दक्षिण की नदी–दीवार से
